title: Judge Puts Limits on Search for Noncitizen Voters
summary:
Elections for Congress are less than two weeks away. A judge in California has put limits on a government search for noncitizens on voter lists.

A voter list, or voter roll, shows who is signed up to vote. In the United States, only citizens may vote in federal elections. Voting by noncitizens is already against the law, and it is extremely rare.

Since August, the Department of Homeland Security, or DHS, has had hundreds of agents looking for voter fraud. The judge said agents cannot stop people for interviews unless they think the person is a noncitizen. The ruling covers nine states, including California, New York and Georgia. The judge worried that DHS lists had mistakes and included citizens.

In another case, the Department of Justice says about 20,000 noncitizens are on California's voter rolls. California officials say they are not sure that list is correct. Another court hearing is set for next Tuesday.
why_it_matters: Fair rules for voting help make sure every citizen's vote counts, including your family's.
